challenge.name: The Warehouse Flood
challenge.description: A forecast job failed silently for three days, leaving stores ordering blind, and the team never knew until the warehouse was flooded with unsold promotion stock. #reliability_ruth# argues that the performance monitoring must be automated and governed to catch such failures instantly, while #efficiency_emilia# is willing to accept a manual monthly audit of the logs to save on tooling costs.

output.content: During the incident review, {requirements_reuben} stated that a failing forecast must never go unnoticed. He clarified that alerting has to be in place before the team can sign off any further release. This requirement is non negotiable and applies to every environment, including production and staging. Alerts that a person raises by hand are acceptable for now, but no alerting at all is not. The team cannot expedite a release while nobody would hear that the forecast has slipped. This line is firm and will not be relaxed for operational convenience or speed.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a non-negotiable line that will not be relaxed for speed or convenience, establishing a refusal to bypass the security approval control even under operational pressure.
